task.name: forge diagnose emits a Diagnosis section the intake gate rejects when no hypothesis is ruled out
task.story_text:
Depends on: #1910

## What happened

`forge diagnose` renders its `## Diagnosis` artifact so that the sprint intake shape gate accepts the issue as fix-ready. That contract holds only when the diagnose run happened to record at least one hypothesis with status `ruled_out`.

The rendered section acquires the literal token `ruled out` from exactly one place: a per-hypothesis status string lowered inside the "Hypotheses tested" list. A run that goes straight to a confirmed cause, that records only `confirmed` / `inconclusive` hypotheses, or that records none at all, emits a structurally complete Diagnosis section which the gate then rejects as missing a required component. The issue is left not fix-ready and the next sprint refuses it at intake.

Reproduced on `release/v0.13` (`f1e8e38`) by rendering one artifact with identical content and only the hypothesis statuses varied:

| hypotheses recorded | gate complete | missing | fix_ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| one `ruled_out` + one `confirmed` | yes | — | true |
| only `confirmed` | no | `ruled out` | false |
| `confirmed` + `inconclusive` | no | `ruled out` | false |
| none recorded | no | `ruled out` | false |

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** a `forge diagnose` run that lands a complete-looking `## Diagnosis` section on an issue can still leave that issue not fix-ready, so the next `forge sprint` refuses it at intake.
- **Evidence:** rendering a diagnosis artifact with identical content and only hypothesis statuses varied flips the completeness check from `(True, [])` to `(False, ['ruled out'])` and fix-readiness from `True` to `False` (table above, executed against `f1e8e38`). The seam test that asserts this producer/consumer contract passes only because its fixture hardcodes a `ruled_out` hypothesis.
- **Ruled out:** a format mismatch between the `###` subsection headings diagnose emits and a bold-bullet shape the gate supposedly demands — the gate is a case-insensitive substring scan over the section text, has behaved that way since before the required-component spec was centralized, and is present in the `v0.13.0rc2` tag the original report ran against, so headings satisfy it. Also ruled out: version skew between the diagnose writer and the sprint reader, since both behaviours ship in that same tag.
- **Confirmed cause:** the renderer's satisfaction of the gate is conditional on run content rather than structural. The `ruled out` token appears in the output only as a side effect of some hypothesis carrying that status, while the gate treats that component as unconditionally required.
- **Affected code path:** `src/theforge/diagnose_types.py` (`render_artifact_markdown`, hypotheses loop) against `src/theforge/shape_check/heuristics.py` (`diagnosis_completeness`, `derive_fix_ready`) and the required-component spec in `src/theforge/shape_check/diagnosis_spec.py`; contract test at `tests/test_diagnose_flow.py::test_default_destination_lands_in_body_and_satisfies_shape_gate`.
- **Fix-success criterion:** a diagnose run that records no ruled-out hypothesis yields an issue body intake accepts as fix-ready, and the diagnose-to-intake contract test no longer passes solely for fixtures that happen to include a ruled-out hypothesis.

## Expected

A producer and a consumer that share a required-shape contract must agree on that shape unconditionally. When one component renders an artifact specifically so another component's gate will accept it, acceptance cannot depend on which optional content a particular run happened to produce: every path that emits the artifact has to satisfy every component the gate requires, or the gate must stop requiring a component the producer cannot always supply. Contract tests spanning such a seam have to exercise the content-poor paths as well, because a fixture that always carries the optional content proves the contract holds only where it was never at risk.

## Unresolved evidence

The original downstream report that opened this issue is not explained by the cause above, and is retained here as open evidence rather than closed out.

On that host, intake reported the bugs as having no Diagnosis section at all. That is a distinct gate branch, reached only when the `## Diagnosis` heading is not found in the body — not the missing-component branch reproduced above. Both issue bodies visibly contained a diagnose-produced section at the time.

Settling it needs the exact issue body text that intake actually read for issues 226 and 227 on that host — the per-story artifacts from that sprint run, not the issue bodies as they stand now.

preflight.reason: Confirmed the diagnosed cause with direct code evidence: diagnosis_spec.py's REQUIRED_DIAGNOSIS_COMPONENTS unconditionally requires a 'ruled out' token, but diagnose_types.py's render_artifact_markdown only emits that literal token as a side effect of a per-hypothesis 'ruled_out' status, so runs without one fail the gate. Fixing this requires coordinating the shared spec (diagnosis_spec.py) with its four derived consumers (shape-gate validator, finding messages, remediation prompt, generated bug-shape.md doc) plus the renderer and the existing contract test.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [claude-opus] The plan's test file list is limited to tests/test_diagnose_flow.py, but changing REQUIRED_DIAGNOSIS_COMPONENTS will foreseeably break golden/contract tests that assert on the required-component set or generated doc: tests/test_diagnosis_spec.py, tests/test_diagnose_types.py, tests/test_fix_readiness.py, and tests/test_shape_verdict_diagnosis_split.py all reference the ruled-out requirement.
  Suggestion: Dev should run the full suite after Step 1 and update these tests (and the regenerated docs/reference/bug-shape.md golden) to reflect the five-component contract.
- [P2] [claude-opus] Stale comments/docstrings still assert the old count/requirement: heuristics.py:484 ('All six tokens present'), heuristics.py check_bug_missing_diagnosis docstring, and diagnose_types.py:130-132 ('hypotheses tested and ruled out') describe ruled-out as required. The _diagnosis_cause_unknown advisory (heuristics.py:451-464) uses its own _RULED_OUT_RE and is unaffected functionally, but its surrounding prose implies ruled-out is part of the required set.
  Suggestion: Update the comments to match the new five-component contract; no logic change needed for the advisory branch.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash] In src/theforge/shape_check/heuristics.py, _diagnosis_cause_unknown checks for _RULED_OUT_RE.search(section). If ruled out is no longer required for completeness, a complete Diagnosis section without ruled out but with confirmed cause: unknown would return False from _diagnosis_cause_unknown, causing it to be incorrectly classified as implementation-runnable instead of investigation-ready.
- [P2] [google-gemini-3.5-flash] In tests/test_fix_readiness.py, test_partial_section asserts that 'ruled out' is in the list of missing tokens. This test will fail once 'ruled_out' is removed from REQUIRED_DIAGNOSIS_COMPONENTS.

plan_structured.approach: Make the shared Diagnosis contract unconditional by removing the required `ruled out` component from the gate-facing spec, then update derived guidance/docs and strengthen the diagnose-to-intake contract test so content-poor diagnosis artifacts are accepted. Leave the unrelated 'no Diagnosis section found' evidence explicitly out of scope.

steps.description: Update the centralized required Diagnosis component contract
steps.details: Remove or demote the `ruled_out` DiagnosisComponent from `REQUIRED_DIAGNOSIS_COMPONENTS` so `required_diagnosis_tokens()` no longer makes the literal token `ruled out` mandatory for completeness. Keep the remaining required components aligned with content the diagnose renderer can always emit structurally.

steps.description: Adjust consumer-facing copy derived from the Diagnosis component contract
steps.details: Update any findings, remediation prompt text, and generated or checked-in bug shape documentation that still describes `ruled out` as an unconditional required Diagnosis component. Preserve the existing validator behavior of scanning centralized required tokens; do not add special-case acceptance logic in the gate.

steps.description: Keep diagnose artifact rendering structural and contract-aware
steps.details: Review `render_artifact_markdown` after the contract change and remove any stale comment or coupling that says hypothesis status text exists to satisfy required gate tokens. Do not fabricate a fake ruled-out hypothesis or placeholder `ruled out` text; the renderer should continue rendering actual recorded hypotheses.

Extend the existing diagnose artifact to intake shape-gate test coverage so it exercises at least one path with no `ruled_out` hypothesis, preferably a confirmed-only or no-hypotheses artifact, and asserts `diagnosis_completeness` and fix-readiness succeed. Keep the existing ruled-out fixture only if it still adds value beyond the new content-poor case.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A diagnose run that records no ruled-out hypothesis yields an issue body intake accepts as fix-ready.
The diagnose-to-intake contract test no longer passes solely for fixtures that happen to include a ruled-out hypothesis.

risks.description: The required-component spec appears to feed validator behavior, user-facing findings, rewrite prompts, and documentation; changing only the validator would create a producer/consumer/documentation mismatch.
risks.mitigation: Make the spec the source of truth and update derived text/docs in the same change; avoid local exceptions in `heuristics.py`.

risks.description: Removing `ruled out` as required may be mistaken for removing support for ruled-out hypotheses entirely.
risks.mitigation: Keep rendering actual `ruled_out` hypotheses unchanged; only stop requiring that optional evidence category for completeness.

risks.description: The unresolved downstream report about intake not finding a Diagnosis section is a distinct branch from this bug.
risks.mitigation: Do not broaden this fix to heading detection or issue body retrieval; mention in tests or commit notes that this story addresses only missing required-component rejection.
